scope: repair diff 9819794..d2173ca plus standing findings R1, R2
note_on_ids: The reviewer returned this finding as 'R1'; renumbered to R3 here to avoid collision with round 1's R1.

findings.claim: The strict `parsed["certify"] is True` correctly closes the over-certify direction but silently introduces the opposite ceiling: a provider response of {"certify": "true"} — a routine string-boolean slip in the CERTIFYING direction — now fails closed, and nothing in any document of record declares it.
findings.evidence: src/browser/judge.py:249. The consequence is named only in an inline code comment (judge.py:239-248). Orchestrator confirmed by grep: no mention in docs/support-matrix.md (D25 covers only 'live grading quality unsupported'), ADR-017 (unmodified by the repair diff), README.md, docs/analysis.md, or tasks/TODO.md's M36 entry. judge-parse-response-strict-boolean's 9 scenarios test only reject-direction strings ('false', 'no', '0') — orchestrator confirmed no scenario supplies the string 'true', so the boundary the fix creates is uncharacterised.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'false-refusal|string-typed|formatting slip' across the documents of record returns no hit for the certify risk; 'true' is True -> False
findings.acceptance: Either (a) a support-matrix D-row names the false-refusal ceiling this strict check introduces, the way D22 names the aggregate guard's, or (b) a scenario pins the string-'true' reject behaviour so the boundary is characterised, or (c) the parser normalises a small explicit set of true-spellings. Absence of all three is the gap.
findings.orchestrator_note: Reproduced independently. Blocks: D22 in this same file is the exact precedent — it declares a false-refusal cost even with no fixture to demonstrate it, and its own text says a 'no case demonstrates this' limitation is a claim about eval coverage, not proof the shape cannot occur. An undeclared over-refusal ceiling has been a blocking finding on this repo three times (PR #25 R2, PR #30 R1, and this). The failure mode here is not subtle: if the chosen model emits string booleans, the agent stops certifying anything at all, and no one can observe what it emits because there is no API key in this environment.
